html:
A thin copper plate dated to the Saka year 822, which is 900 CE, recording that a family's debt had been cancelled. It is the oldest known written document from the Philippines.

A labourer found it in 1987 while dredging near the mouth of the Lumbang River in Laguna, on Luzon. The Dutch scholar Antoon Postma read it in 1992. The text is in Old Malay, written in the Kawi script of Java, with Sanskrit and Old Javanese words. It names a lady called Angkatan and her family, freed from a debt in gold, and it mentions places that seem to include Tondo.

Before this find, the earliest Philippine writing anyone knew of came after the Spanish arrived in 1521. The plate shows that Luzon already had rulers, scribes, legal records and links to the Malay speaking world of Srivijaya and Java six centuries earlier. It is now in the National Museum in Manila. Compare the much later printed Doctrina Christiana.
sum: A thin copper plate dated to the Saka year 822, which is 900 CE, recording that a family's debt had been cancelled. It is the oldest known written document from the Philippines.
